These are model picks, not locks. At standard −110 odds a bet has to win 52.4% of the time just to break even. In testing, the model's picks won about 54–56%, which means plenty of losing weeks.

Best prices by expected return

Every game

Predicted score comes from the model: team ratings for scoring, play-by-play efficiency, returning production and roster talent, updated with every game played.
Hit % follows the model's side. For spreads and totals it's how often the model's side actually won at that size of edge (2019–2025); for moneylines it's the model's win chance from its predicted margin. A moneyline only counts as a good price if a market-blended check agrees, since the model alone is overconfident on long shots.
Return per $100 is the average result if you made this bet many times: hit % × payout, minus the stake. Moneylines use the best price found across sportsbooks; spreads and totals assume standard −110.
QB alerts flag teams whose usual starting quarterback missed their last game or has shared time. The model does not adjust for this yet, so check those games before betting.
Best bets by expected return (the ranked list) did not beat the sportsbooks in testing; it is mainly useful for finding the best price. The model's best bets above follow the rules that did hold up in testing.
Line status: "Bet now" means the gap between the model and the current line still meets the rules. "Line moved" means the number has shifted since it opened and most of the edge is gone.
New model, still raw. On 2023–26 games it never saw, its predicted margins missed by 10.3 points on average, against 9.7 for the Vegas spread, so Vegas is the sharper number. The game predictions are here for reference, not as bets.
Player props are tested against about 18,700 real lines: picks the model rates 54%+ actually won about 54–59%. That's only profitable at a fair price, so each pick shows the worst price still worth taking.

Best player props

Only props the model likes, at most one per player, never forced. Skipped automatically: players with fewer than 3 games this season, anyone listed questionable or worse, and props where the model is far from the line (usually news it doesn't know).

Every game: model vs Vegas

Predicted score comes from team ratings for scoring and play-by-play efficiency (EPA), adjusted for opponents and weighted toward recent games, with last season carried into this one.
Win % converts the model's margin into a win chance (NFL games land about 13.5 points from the expected margin on average).
Hit % on props is the realistic chance, calibrated on 2024–25 real lines and confirmed on this season's: the raw model is overconfident. Only Strong picks (56%+) are posted.
New model, still raw. Tested against about 4,800 real ESPN BET lines from 2024 and 2025. Props the model rated 70% or higher won about 65% in both seasons (break-even at normal prices is about 52–54%). The 65–70% group won 56–62%. Below 65% it didn't beat the line, so it makes no picks there.
Unlike the NBA and NFL, college books often miss: the model's biggest disagreements with the line did best. Still check injuries and depth charts, since the model can't see who's starting.

Best college props

Only Strong props are posted: model 70%+ (won about 61–80% in testing). Max 3 per game, one per player, never forced.

Find a player

Projection = expected volume (attempts, carries, catches; recent games weighted more) × efficiency × how much the opponent gives up, adjusted with the CFB game model's predicted score for this game.
Hit % is how often props in that confidence band actually won against real lines in 2024–25, not the model's raw number.
Chances, not locks. The model rates every player from his recent rounds, then plays out the rest of the tournament 20,000 times (cut included), in two independently built models whose chances are averaged, to get each player's chance to win, finish top 5 / 10 / 20 and make the cut.
No sportsbook golf lines come in automatically, so the model can't tell you which bets are good value on its own. Use Check a line with the odds your book offers: a bet is only worth it when the book pays more than the model's fair odds.

The whole field

Rating = how many strokes better or worse than an average tour player he scores per round, after adjusting every round for how hard the course played that day. Recent rounds count more; players with few rounds are pulled toward average.
Round score and birdies are for the player's next round he hasn't started, using how the course has played this week (or last year's event before round 1). The line check uses how far real rounds landed from the projection in 2025–26, not a guess.
Tested on 2025–26:
College football only for now. Build a regular parlay (legs from different games) or a same-game parlay. The site shows the model's chance that the whole thing hits, and whether the payout is worth it.
Parlays usually favor the house: its cut grows with every leg, and a 4-leg parlay hits far less often than it feels like it should. Same-game legs move together: a QB's passing yards and his top receiver's yards rise and fall together, so the site adjusts for that.

Suggested 2-pick for this game

Each leg's chance is the site's tested chance: model picks at 70%+ won 61–75% against real lines in 2024 and 2025. Legs the model is less sure about are shown near a coin flip (about 53%), because in testing they barely beat the line.
How legs move together was learned from every player-game in 2022–24 box scores and checked on 2025 games the model never saw: for two strong legs in the same game it said 47.3% and they hit together 48.3% of the time. Different games are treated as unrelated.
PrizePicks payouts shown are the standard ones (Power: 2 picks 3×, 3 picks 5×, 4 picks 10×, 5 picks 20×, 6 picks 37.5×; Flex varies). They change by state and promotion, so check your app. Every PrizePicks entry needs players from at least two teams.

Every player tonight

Projection = expected minutes × the player's per-minute production (recent games weighted more), adjusted for how much the opponent gives up to his position and for the pace of both teams. Players listed as out are removed.
Hit % blends the model with the sportsbook's own price. Tested against about 3,700 real prop lines, the model alone was overconfident (it leaned hard on unders that hit less often than it thought), while the market's price was accurate. The blend uses mostly the market plus the model's opinion. The "Check a line" box shows the model alone.
Expected return is hit % × payout, minus the stake, per bet. Prices are DraftKings' (from Nov 7 the NBA tab uses DraftKings lines only). On PrizePicks the same pick needs about 58% to break even, so check that the model's chance clears that before playing it there.
